newsitem.title: POLAND: IMI unit sees Polish CPI at 14 pct in '97.
newsitem.headline: IMI unit sees Polish CPI at 14 pct in '97.

text.p: The IMI Sigeco UK Ltd, part of the IMI Group, forecast Polish year-on-year inflation at 14 percent in 1997 against 18.5 percent in 1996, it said in its country report dated March 14.
In February the index was at 17.3 percent.
It said that any changes in economic policy after this year's parliamentary polls, due around September, would come too late to affect growth in 1997, which IMI said would remain flat at 6.0 percent.

IMI said exports would increase 10 percent in 1997 against 6.7 percent last year, as competitive German exports and industrial output would be slow to recover and also because of improving demand from Russia and the Ukraine.
It said imports would increase 23 percent this year after a 31.8 percent rise in 1996, which would widen the current account trade deficit to $13.2 billion from $8.1 billion.
IMI said that the overall current account deficit would widen to $4 billion this year from $1.4 billion in 1996.
The report said the stronger export growth should translate into faster industrial output growth, which IMI expected to reach 10 percent in 1997 after a 8.8 percent rise last year.
IMI said investment should grow 19 percent this year after 21.6 percent growth last year.
